title: When the Wardrobe Sings
premise: Xanthe Halloran, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost the ability to taste twelve years ago, has built a career on elegant evasion—reviews that praise everything and commit to nothing. When their childhood home, Halloran House, is put up for auction by an estranged aunt, Xanthe returns to catalogue its contents and finds their late mother's wardrobe humming with recorded voices: family recipes dictated as lullabies, arguments, confessions, including the truth of why Xanthe's sense of taste died the same night their father left. As the auction date closes in and developers circle, Xanthe must transcribe, translate, and finally speak aloud what the wardrobe has been singing—and choose whether to let the house go or inherit the grief that comes with keeping it. The novel ends with Xanthe publishing one honest review, tasting nothing but saying everything, as the house passes to strangers who will hear the songs anyway.
about_author: Marguerite Eriksen is the pen name of a former line cook turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories in coastal New England. She writes about houses that remember more than the people who leave them.

chapters.title: The Palate of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Xanthe files another glowing, empty review from a restaurant they cannot taste, then receives a certified letter: Halloran House enters auction in thirty days. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: numb competence cracking into dread—the past arriving as paperwork.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Departure
chapters.summary: Xanthe returns to the shuttered house to appraise contents for the estate sale, walking rooms that smell of cedar and old rain. They find their mother's wardrobe locked with a brass key on Xanthe's own keyring. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: uncanny homecoming; grief mistaken for nostalgia.

chapters.title: What the Cedar Remembers
chapters.summary: Opening the wardrobe, Xanthe hears faint singing—a woman's voice reciting measurements like recipes. Their aunt Sable arrives unannounced, hostile, insisting everything be sold fast and untouched. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: wonder shadowed by suspicion; first hint Sable knows what's inside.

chapters.title: Recipes for a Lullaby
chapters.summary: At night the wardrobe sings clearly: Xanthe's mother dictating recipes interleaved with fragments of memory—flour, salt, 'and don't tell the child.' Xanthe begins recording the songs, tasting phantom flavors for the first time in years. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: hunger returning as haunting.

chapters.title: Sable's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV: she reveals the debts that forced the auction and her resentment of the mother who willed the house 'to whoever listens.' She warns Xanthe that the last song destroyed their father. Emotional beat: antagonist humanized; the inheritance revealed as a burden, not a gift.

chapters.title: The Night of the Burnt Sugar
chapters.summary: A recorded argument surfaces: the night Xanthe's taste died, their father burned a caramel he'd promised to make, and left mid-sentence. The wardrobe holds his unfinished apology. Xanthe, shaken, nearly sells the key to a dealer. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: rising tension; temptation to stay silent forever.

chapters.title: Bidders at the Gate
chapters.summary: Developers tour the house; the auction looms in ten days. Xanthe cooks their mother's recovered recipes for Sable, and both taste something impossible—memory made edible. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: tentative alliance; the sisters-in-law sharing a table instead of a battlefield.

chapters.title: The Untranslatable Sentence
chapters.summary: The final recording: the mother's voice completing the father's broken sentence—an admission that she drove him away to protect Xanthe from his cruelty, and asked the wardrobe to keep singing until someone could bear it. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: climax; devastation and release fused.

chapters.title: Lot Forty-One
chapters.summary: Auction day. Xanthe lets the house go to a young couple who pause at the wardrobe and hear it hum. Sable signs the papers weeping; Xanthe takes only the recordings and the brass key. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: surrender as choice; survival's price paid consciously at last.

chapters.title: An Honest Review
chapters.summary: Months later, Xanthe publishes a review that admits everything—'I taste nothing, and this meal was still beautiful'—ending their career of almost-saying-it. In a rented kitchen they cook the final recipe aloud, teaching it to the new owners by phone. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: resolution; inheritance carried forward as voice, not walls.
